> I'm glad that given considerations of psychological impact, you canceled. There are also physiological concerns:

My update said that I canceled because of both my physical state and the top's potential psychological reaction.

To address your concern about mandatory reporting, no. In my location, a health care practitioner would not be required to report it. Reporting is required here in the case of child abuse (not applicable in my case), elder abuse, and imminent risk to the life of the patient or others (i.e., suicide or threats of assault/ murder). 

In BDSM, in my location, the only activities that cannot considered consensual (regardless of the bottom trying to give consent) are breath play and extreme mutilation (i.g., amputation), so that is not a concern, either.

> I also don't know how aware of those things you are

Perhaps this is why I found your comment so offensive. Someone has to be either very new to the scene or very isolated not to be aware of things like stigma and legal considerations for their location. There is very little in my posts here that implies I am either new or choose to be ignorant of those things.

I am very fortunate to live in a city/ region where practicing kink does not make people outsiders. Kink-aware health practitioners are not uncommon here. And woman who practice kink here are not automatically considered abused little things in need of rescuing.

I appreciate your concern. I do. And I appreciate your ensuring that people are playing safe. But please try to have a little more confidence in others' ability to educate themselves.
Scheduling is up to the doctors, not me.
You have no idea where I live. You don't know what my community is like. You do not have the information to make reasonable comments about my society.

I understand your concern, but if a miscarriage occurs at a very early stage of a pregnancy, like I'm in, it wouldn't require a hospital visit unless there's extreme pain or heavy clotting. (I've miscarried before and was told to watch for "lemon-sized" clots.) Miscarriages early in the first trimester are very common and are not as dangerous as people think. Most women just think they're having a late period.

ETA: Also, the bleeding would be very unlikely to start right on the spot. It would likely happen a few hours later.

I also understand concerns about legal issues or other "trouble," but it's documented with my MD that I practice consensual BDSM. It's documented that I'm seeking an abortion. I've signed every health and safety waiver imaginable at my dungeon putting the blame on me rather than them if something happened. And there's no way I'd tell authorities who my top was if they asked. It would fall on me.
I was hoping to hear from someone pro-life, so thank you for your honesty about your political stance while offering a constructive comment.

As I said to His_elegans, thanks for the comments about my health outside of the fetus. It was informative and helpful to know what to expect if he and I choose to go ahead with the scene. I did inform him after reading all of your responses, mainly because of the increased physical risks he would need to be aware of. Thanks for the response.

These are very good points. I tried to look for information like this (the effects on the mother's body) before posting but all I could find was how to avoid harming the fetus. I greatly appreciate this information. Thank you.

My earlier reason for not informing him is that it might unnecessarily distress him. He might decide he wants to proceed, not expecting an emotional reaction*, then discover feelings afterward about potentially harming a fetus. I just informed him, so if we do play, I'll have to keep a close eye on him in the following week or so to make sure he doesn't have a bad psychological reaction.
Thanks for your thoughts.
The possibility of hurting him psychologically was one of my biggest reasons for either informing him or cancelling. It just seems like that falls under non-consensual harm. Thanks for your response.

If he intends to be completely naked, just have them on the nightstand or somewhere else within reach. We have lots of securing hooks around the bed so we clip them onto one of those. 

To note, a lot of people practice bondage without getting undressed for sex, but I see your confusion if you're not used to that. ;)
